title: From Silk Routes to the Digital Frontier: The Rahmanan Family's Vision for the Future of Rug Collecting
summary: In the world of fine rugs and textiles, the name Rahmanan has long been synonymous with an almost academic devotion to the art of the loom. For decades, the family has operated at the intersection of history and artistry, moving between the silent majesty of museum quality antiques and the fast paced demands of contemporary interior design. Now, with the launch of RugsOnNet.com , the family is consolidating their multi generational expertise into a single, comprehensive digital powerhouse.

title: Christie's to auction master Hiroshige woodblock print collection in September
summary: Over the course of half a century, the American businessman Alan Medaugh has assembled one of the largest and greatest collections of woodblock prints by the master of the medium, Utagawa Hiroshige (1797-1858). Now, this group of more than 600 sheets, many of the absolute greatest rarity, quality, and state of preservation focusing on the earliest impressions, showing the most vibrant color. comes to auction at Christie's Rockefeller Center 15 September 2026; on view 11-14 September. Hiroshige: Colors of the Four Seasons, the Alan Medaugh Collection, is the first of what promises to be a three-sale series. This first sale will include more than 180 prints that span the artist's career and demonstrate the remarkable breadth of his artistic achievement. title: Woody Auction will greet autumn with an American Brilliant Cut Glass auction
summary: Fans of American Brilliant Cut Glass (ABCG) need to mark their calendars for Saturday, September 19, beginning at 9:30 am Central Time. That’s when Woody Auction will burst into autumn with a fun sale featuring nearly 300 lots, each offered without reserve. The auction will be held online and live in the Woody auction hall at 130 East 3rd Street in Douglass. One of the highlights of this auction event is its unique connection to the legendary American pianist, singer, actor, and flamboyant entertainer Liberace, famed for blending classical technique with pop appeal. Keen observers will discover a stunning pair of candelabra that are identical in form to a single candelabrum that was sold during the renowned 1988 Liberace Estate Auction. “As always, we invite everyone to experience the excitement of auction day by joining us in person,” said Jason Woody of Woody Auction. “This

title: William Dobson Self-Portrait will bring young people together on UK Tour
summary: On International Youth Day, Tate and the National Portrait Gallery announce a national tour of William Dobson’s Self-Portrait c.1635-40. Focused on bringing together young people across the country, the forthcoming tour will connect this significant 17th century painting to a new generation. Jointly acquired in 2025 by Tate and the National Portrait Gallery, throughout 2027 the portrait will tour to Hull’s Ferens Art Gallery and Oxford’s Ashmolean before returning to London to be shown at the National Portrait Gallery. The tour and supporting programme has been made possible from The National Lottery Heritage Fund, alongside generous support from Bjorn Saven CBE, David and Emma Verey Charitable Trust and Tavolozza Foundation. title: New publication explores history of science collections
summary: Published by Princeton University Press in association with The Huntington, Worlds Unfolding: Science on the Page is designed for readers within and beyond the sciences, pairing vivid images with concise texts that explore the history of science through questions, comparisons, and unexpected juxtapositions. Images of medieval maps, botanical specimens, scientific instruments, lightbulbs, anatomical drawings, X-ray photographs, rare books, and archival documents are accompanied by extended captions that show how scientific knowledge has been recorded, shared, and challenged across time and place. The publication will be available Oct. 13, 2026, at the Huntington Store, from Princeton University Press, and through online distributors. “At The Huntington, we see every day how collections are catalysts for discovery,” said Sandra Brooke Gordon, Avery Director of the Library at The Huntington. “Worlds Unfolding brings that

title: Heritage Auctions to feature rare Latin American coins at ANA World & Ancient event
summary: Private collections, including one of the finest troves of Latin American Crowns ever assembled, will produce many of the top offerings at Heritage's ANA World & Ancient Coins Platinum Session and Signature® Auction Sept. 1-5. The Grundy Collection of Latin American and Spanish Coins includes nearly 200 lots, many of which are among the top-graded coins from numerous countries throughout Central and South America, prioritizing historical importance, rarity, provenance and condition. The collection is extraordinary — a focused, scholarly collection of the type that advanced Latin American numismatics collectors value most. Latin American coinage spans more than four centuries of production at colonial and independent republic mints that emerged in the 19th century. title: Chinese artist Liu Wei to create new sculptures for The Met's Fifth Avenue Facade
summary: This fall, The Metropolitan Museum of Art will unveil a new suite of sculptures by Liu Wei (born 1972, Beijing, China) in the niches of its Fifth Avenue facade, marking the artist’s first major project in the United States and The Met’s first presentation of a commissioned work by an artist from China since 2006. Widely recognized for his ambitious sculptures and installations that examine processes of transformation, urbanization, and social change, Liu will create four monumental works that respond to both the Museum’s architecture and the encyclopedic scope of its collection. Through a dynamic visual language of assemblage and reconfiguration, the project explores the continual reshaping of historical and contemporary experience through rupture and healing. The Genesis Facade Commission: Liu Wei, Speculation will be on view from September 17, 2026, through June 8, 2027. “Liu Wei’s sculptures for The Genesis Facade Commission are sure to reflect

title: Birmingham Museum of Art opens Wall to Wall: Christopher Myers
summary: The Birmingham Museum of Art presents Wall to Wall: Christopher Myers, the fifth installment of the Museum’s ongoing Wall to Wall series. Created specifically for the BMA, the monumental installation, The Slow Can Beat the Quick, by New York-based artist and writer Christopher Myers transforms the Museum’s lobby with a work inspired by Birmingham’s histories of steel, labor, and land. “With the first textile installation commissioned for Wall to Wall, Christopher Myers demonstrates how textiles can hold history, memory, and identity, and his work transforms the Museum's main lobby into a space that is monumental but also intimate, and deeply connected to Birmingham's past and present,” says Jade Powers, Hugh Kaul Curator of Contemporary Art. title: Ingleby features Chilean painter Sebastián Espejo in new Feast Room exhibition
summary: Coinciding with the 2026 Edinburgh Art Festival, Ingleby presents its next ‘Instalment' in the gallery’s Feast Room, with the Chilean painter Sebastián Espejo. Stepping into Espejo’s studio, currently located on the edge of an industrial estate in Northeast London, is a surprising experience. Despite a slightly dispiriting approach, past industrial bakeries and a recycling centre, the studio itself emits a friendly glow. There is a smell of cedar, the sound of Tropicália, and the taste of nuts and dark chocolate figs offered from a traditional Chilean woven basket. Sebastián brews herbal tea and gestures to a seat, it's a haven in the thick of London’s urban sprawl. Looking around the studio, it’s clear that Sebastian is a collector. Occupying every surface are objects that have travelled with the artist from other times and places - loyal companions as he calls them “...characters in a miniature theatre of light. title: Franz Gertsch retrospective brings six decades of monumental painting to Bern
summary: The Kunstmuseum Bern is presenting a major retrospective devoted to Franz Gertsch, bringing together around 40 paintings that trace more than six decades of work by one of Switzerland’s most influential postwar artists. Franz Gertsch. Blow-Up (Part I) opens on August 14, 2026, and remains on view through January 17, 2027. A second part of the retrospective will open at the Museum Franz Gertsch in Burgdorf on September 19. Gertsch, who died in 2022 at the age of 92, became internationally known for monumental paintings that occupy an unusual territory between photographic precision and painterly abstraction. Developed by the Louisiana Museum of Modern Art in close collaboration with the artist and his family, Blow-Up was subsequently shown at the Deichtorhallen Hamburg. title: Matthias Noggler wins 2026 RLB Art Prize in Tyrol
summary: Matthias Noggler has been named the winner of the 2026 RLB Art Prize, one of Tyrol’s established awards for emerging and mid-career contemporary artists. The two recognition prizes went to Vik Bayer and Simona Obholzer. Presented by Raiffeisen-Landesbank Tirol, the biennial prize has supported artists connected to Tyrol since 2004. This year’s edition also marks a significant expansion of the program: the main award has increased from €10,000 to €15,000, while each recognition prize has risen from €4,000 to €6,000. The age limit for applicants was also raised from 40 to 45. A total of 95 artists applied for the 2026 edition. Eligible artists had to have been born in Tyrol or maintain their primary residence there. Noggler, who was born in Innsbruck in 1990 and now lives in Berlin, was selected for a painting practice that moves freely across a wide range of art-historical references. title: Columbia Museum of Art exhibition celebrates deep connection between craft and body
summary: The Columbia Museum of Art presents featured exhibition Body Matters, on view August 22, 2026, through January 3, 2027. Organized by the CMA, this exclusive exhibition explores the reciprocal relationship between craft objects and the people who make and use them. Opening day festivities include a Member Morning as well as an afternoon conversation between CMA Curator Sadé Ayorinde and featured artist Judy Moonelis. The human body is essential to craft. This genre of art is rooted in physical labor, tactile knowledge, and material intimacy, and the resulting pieces are often intended to protect bodies or to assist in nourishing them. title: Shin Gallery opens collaborative drawing exhibition The Enduring Line
summary: Drawing is the most elemental act in art. Long before an idea becomes a painting, sculpture, installation, or performance, it often first emerges as a mark on paper—a line searching for form. Foundational works of drawing are often where the most intimate moments with an artist begin, offering a unique window into their minds where subjects are depicted out of instinct rather than obligation. In celebration of drawing, Shin Gallery is presenting The Enduring Line, a collaborative, thought-provoking exhibition on view from August 1st to September 26, 2026. Presenting works by artists whose approaches to drawing are as diverse as their histories, this exhibition brings the physical emergence of ideas to the forefront of the artistic conversation. title: Film Forum to host US theatrical premiere of Paula González-Nasser's The Scout
summary: Film Forum will present the U.S. theatrical premiere of Paula González-Nasser’s The Scout on Friday, September 25. Director González-Nasser spent six years working as a location scout. In this luminous directorial debut, she brings us into a day in the life of a young scout tasked with finding the perfect interiors for a television pilot. Sofía (Mimi Davila) moves in and out of other people’s intimate spaces and quotidian lives, tweaking her personality just enough to connect while struggling to find balance between her professional and personal worlds. With a mounting stack of parking tickets and the impertinent commentaries of her crew, she faces a series of small-yet-paralyzing obstacles that render her day increasingly exhausting. Through a constellation of quiet but poignant vignettes, the film offers an original view into the invisible

title: Abdelrahman Alkahlout wins inaugural James Nachtwey Prize for Gaza photography
summary: The Photo Journalism Prize announced Palestinian photojournalist Abdelrahman Alkahlout as the recipient of the inaugural James Nachtwey Prize for his photographic series, Echoes of Genocide: Gaza’s Civilian Suffering. Selected personally by internationally renowned photojournalist James Nachtwey, the €5,000 prize recognizes photographic work of exceptional courage, humanity and journalistic significance. Created in Nachtwey’s name, the award honors photographers who bear witness to defining events of our time and bring sustained attention to the lives of those affected by conflict, displacement and humanitarian crisis. Through Echoes of Genocide: Gaza’s Civilian Suffering, Alkahlout documents the human consequences of the war in Gaza. His photographs move beyond the scale of destruction to focus on the individuals living

title: Forest Lawn Museum highlights relationship between Walt Disney and Hubert Eaton
summary: Forest Lawn Museum proudly presents “California Visionaries: The Lives and Legacies of Walt Disney and Hubert Eaton.” The exhibition is the first to explore the personal and creative relationship between Walt Disney and Forest Lawn Memorial-Parks founder Hubert Eaton, highlighting the philosophical and artistic parallels that shaped their respective legacies and the iconic parks they created. More than mere businessmen, Disney and Eaton traveled similar paths from Missouri to California, opening organizations that are deeply woven into the fabric of American culture. They met in the 1930s, forming a lasting relationship and inspiring one another throughout their careers. In 1966, Disney was an honorary pallbearer at Eaton’s funeral. title: Building an Audience: Timothy Hawkinson Gallery announces an exhibition of works by Brad Eberhard
summary: Can art be fully realized in a vacuum, alone? Is an audience required to complete the circuit, to define and prove its existence? While frequently made alone, there is so often the intention to communicate something personal to others. To bridge a gap and connect. Brad Eberhard has been making paintings and ceramic sculptures that are complex in their construction and intimately scaled, hovering between abstraction to figuration. The compositional rhythms of shapes and colors, as well as the emergence of representational content, grow intuitively. The works are adjacent to self-portraiture, in their revelations of Eberhard’s unique constellations of visual associations. They open brief glimpses into an internal library of accumulated ideas assembled over a lifetime. The contexts and connotations influencing how he sees the world unfold. Allusions

title: Dolby Chadwick Gallery to present solo exhibition by Ian Kimmerly
summary: Dolby Chadwick Gallery will present Some Quieter Melody, an exhibition of recent paintings by San Francisco–based artist Ian Kimmerly, on view throughout September. Confident brushstrokes, constellations of color, and figures rendered through fragments and repetition converge in Kimmerly's latest works, creating mesmerizing, layered compositions whose meanings emerge over time. Kimmerly holds a sustained interest in the intricacies of human connection. A thread of intimate, familiar, and evocative depictions can be traced throughout his practice. In this body of work, he shifts his lens to the ruptures in our bonds, caused by economic and political systems that benefit from division, and to the meaning and beauty we create from our increasing fragmentation. The exhibition title quotes Polish writer and activist Olga Tokarczuk.

title: Skywalker Grill to debut as the signature dining destination at the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art
summary: On Tuesday, September 22, 2026, Los Angeles will welcome a new dining destination with the debut of Skywalker Grill, the signature full-service restaurant atop the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art. Designed by Rockwell Group and operated by Rhubarb Events & Hospitality Collection, part of Oak View Group (OVG), Skywalker Grill draws inspiration from the welcoming spirit of George Lucas' legendary Skywalker Ranch, pairing classic American cuisine with warm hospitality and sweeping views overlooking Los Angeles. Open to both museum visitors and the public, Skywalker Grill welcomes guests for lunch, dinner and weekend brunch, offering a natural extension of a museum visit as well as a place to gather for an evening meal. Remaining open beyond museum hours, the restaurant invites guests to enjoy panoramic views of Los

title: VeneKlasen to host Raphaela Simon's first New York solo show in eight years
summary: VeneKlasen, New York, will present Raphaela Simon: On the Street, the artist's first solo exhibition in New York in over eight years, featuring a selection of recent paintings and sculptures. Inspired by the urban landscape, the works in the exhibition reflect Simon's ongoing engagement with the city—particularly Berlin, where she lives and works. Reducing her subjects to basic geometric forms, stripes, and broad planes of color, Simon distills familiar urban motifs to the point of near illegibility. Her paintings and fabric sculptures alike hover between abstraction and representation, never fully resolving into either. In her fabric sculptures, Simon translates the layered surfaces and fragmented imagery of her paintings into soft, three-dimensional forms, emphasizing the tension between flatness and volume. title: Alexander Gray Associates announces tribute exhibition to sculptor Melvin Edwards
summary: Alexander Gray Associates presents People Make Art: A Tribute to Melvin Edwards, an exhibition that explores the life and practice of the acclaimed sculptor through the work of fifteen artists who knew him. Rather than attempting to define the full scope of Edwards’s (b.1937, Houston, TX; d.2026, Baltimore, MD) artistic community, the show traces one constellation within a far larger universe of relationships, illuminating the generosity, curiosity, and spirit of exchange that animated his work for more than six decades. Featuring paintings, sculptures, and works on paper from 1954 to 2024, People Make Art reflects the extraordinary breadth of Edwards’s artistic engagement and the enduring vitality of his artistic community. The exhibition takes its title from one of Edwards’s characteristically direct observations: “Art doesn't make art, people make art.” The remark

title: Sullivan+Strumpf announce representation of Atong Atem
summary: Sullivan+Strumpf announced their representation of South Sudanese Australian artist Atong Atem, known for her richly staged images that explore photography as a space where history, memory, performance and imagination converge. Drawing on Dinka philosophy, African studio photography, family archives and diverse spiritual and visual traditions, Atem (b.1991), reimagines portraiture as a site of self-determination, where inherited histories are continually reconfigured rather than simply preserved. The announcement comes at a significant juncture in Atom’s career, with her first-ever major institutional solo exhibition, Passage: The Art of Atong Atem, set to open at the National Gallery of Victoria 30 October 2026 until 14 June 2027; premiering new works alongside a comprehensive survey of the past decade of the artist’s practice. title: Exhibition of Japanese art illuminates 500 years of metal mastery
summary: The Dallas Museum of Art premiered Samurai to the Imperial Court: Japanese Metalwork, an exhibition tracing five centuries of metal art in Japan. Through more than 90 works of art drawn from the DMA’s significant holdings and other leading collections, including The Ann & Gabriel Barbier-Mueller Museum: The Samurai Collection, Dallas, Samurai to the Imperial Court celebrates the technical mastery, innovative spirit and aesthetic brilliance of Japanese metal artists. From samurai arms and armor to imperial court commissions, from luminous enameled vessels to sculptures of fantastical animals and figures, this exhibition highlights a dazzling array of objects shaped by centuries of imagination and craftsmanship. The exhibition will remain on view through September 6, 2026. Metalworking has been an integral part of Japanese culture
